hook.text: A home router serves ten devices. An office Wi-Fi network serves thousands. The engineering is completely different.

buildup.text: Enterprise access points are centrally managed. A controller assigns channels, power levels, and security policies.

discovery.text: 802.1X authentication checks each user against a directory like Active Directory before granting access.

twist.text: Radio resource management prevents nearby access points from interfering with each other — auto-tuning in real time.

climax.text: Stadium Wi-Fi handles 60,000 fans streaming simultaneously. Hundreds of access points, carefully planned and tuned.

punchline.text: Enterprise Wi-Fi is an engineering discipline, not a consumer product.

quiz.question: What does 802.1X provide for enterprise Wi-Fi?
options: Individual user authentication against a directory service
Faster download speeds for all devices

details.summary: Enterprise Wi-Fi uses centrally managed access points, controller-based architecture, and features like seamless roaming, VLAN segmentation, RADIUS authentication, and RF management.
details.whyItMatters: Enterprise Wi-Fi design principles explain how large venues provide reliable connectivity to thousands of users. The technology behind corporate and campus networks is fundamentally different from home setups.
takeaways: Controllers manage and configure many access points centrally
802.1X RADIUS authentication secures per-user network access
Seamless roaming hands clients between access points transparently

faq.question: How does enterprise Wi-Fi handle roaming?
faq.answer: Standards like 802.11r enable fast roaming by pre-authenticating with the next access point before disconnecting from the current one. The controller coordinates handoffs so clients experience no interruption.

faq.question: What is the role of a wireless controller?
faq.answer: The controller centrally manages configuration, firmware, RF power levels, and channel assignments for all access points. It enforces security policies, distributes client load, and detects rogue access points.
